content: QRICH1, also referred to as Glutamine-rich protein 1, is a human protein encoded by the QRICH1 gene. A key structural feature of this protein is the presence of a Caspase Activation Recruitment Domain (CARD domain). This domain suggests that QRICH1 plays a role in pathways related to apoptosis, inflammation, and the host immune response. The QRICH1 gene spans 64,363 base pairs and produces an mRNA transcript that is 3,331 base pairs in length. It is located on chromosome 3p21.31, with its genomic sequence starting at base pair 49,057,531 and ending at base pair 49,141,201. The gene contains 11 exons. The precise biological function of QRICH1 remains unclear. However, the presence of the CARD domain near the N-terminal region of the protein implies its involvement in apoptosis and inflammatory processes. QRICH1 is predicted to localize to the nucleus and has been shown to interact with proteins such as ATXN1 (Ataxin-1) and ATF7IP (Activating Transcription Factor 7-Interacting Protein). The QRICH1 protein is composed of 776 amino acids, with glutamine residues making up 14% of its sequence (109 residues). It contains three distinct domains: 1. The CARD domain, which belongs to the death fold superfamily, is implicated in signaling pathways related to apoptosis, immune responses, inflammation, and host defense mechanisms. 2. A glutamine-rich domain, which constitutes the majority of the protein and is highly conserved across orthologs. 3. A Domain of Unknown Function (DUF3504), located near the C-terminal end of the protein sequence. All three domains are well conserved among strict orthologs. Bioinformatics tools have predicted several features of QRICH1: The molecular weight of the protein is approximately 86.5 kDa. Its isoelectric point is 5.59. Post-translational modifications include multiple phosphorylation sites. PhosphoSitePlus has identified three phosphorylated serine residues at positions 343, 345, and 659. Additionally, the NetPhos program predicts 45 phosphorylation sites on serine, threonine, and tyrosine residues. A sulfinated tyrosine is predicted at position 725. No signal peptide or signal peptide cleavage sites are predicted. QRICH1 interacts with proteins such as ATXN1 and ATF7IP. ATXN1 is involved in RNA binding and may play a role in RNA metabolism, while ATF7IP functions as a recruiter protein that links transcription factors to the general transcription machinery, influencing transcription regulation and chromatin organization. QRICH1 is expressed at a level 3.3 times higher than the average gene and is ubiquitously expressed throughout the human body. However, its expression is particularly elevated in tissues such as the thymus, testis, cerebellar cortex, trachea, and embryonic tissues. High QRICH1 expression has also been observed in certain pathological conditions, including germ cell tumors, leukemia, lymphoma, and chondrosarcoma. In terms of evolutionary conservation, QRICH1 is highly conserved among mammalian orthologs and other chordates, including fish, birds, and amphibians. Some conservation is observed in insects, but no orthologs have been identified in plants, fungi, or yeast. QRICH1 has five paralogs, all of which encode zinc finger proteins.
